root_cause.text: Incorrect classification of plain extents as interlaced instead of shifted due to only checking physical start alignment, not physical length alignment, allowing unaligned physical lengths to cause out-of-bounds read in z_erofs_transform_plain().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)` to `!((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)`, requiring both physical address and physical length to be block-aligned. Commit message states: "Only plain data whose start position and on-disk physical length are both aligned to the block size should be classified as interlaced plain extents." CVE description confirms syzbot crafted image with unaligned physical lengths causing OOB read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a local block mask variable to avoid recalculating `sb->s_blocksize - 1` multiple times.
intent_record.what: Added a new local variable `bmask` initialized to `sb->s_blocksize - 1` in the function `z_erofs_map_blocks_ext`.
intent_record.how: The variable `bmask` likely replaces repeated calculations of the block mask, improving runtime efficiency and code clarity in subsequent block-alignment operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix interlaced compression detection by ensuring extent start and length are block-aligned, and reorder operations to use the cleaned m_plen.
intent_record.what: Moved the partial flag setting and masking of m_plen to before the fmt/algorithmformat selection, and changed the condition for interlaced compression from '!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)' to '!((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)'.
intent_record.how: The partial bit is now cleared from m_plen before it is used in the new condition, which correctly checks that both the physical address and the length are block-aligned before choosing interlaced compression.

relevance_review.reason: The change only introduces a local variable to avoid recalculating sb->s_blocksize - 1, which is a minor optimization or readability improvement. It does not address the core issue of incorrect classification due to missing physical length alignment check.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the interlaced compression detection to check both extent start and length alignment, which was previously missing the length check leading to incorrect classification.

candidates.rationale: This condition only checks physical start alignment, not physical length alignment, causing plain extents with unaligned lengths to be incorrectly classified as interlaced instead of shifted, leading to an out-of-bounds read in z_erofs_transform_plain().
